title: Cryptographic Solutions

header.html: 1.3 Explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Encryption: symmetric and asymmetric

Encryption turns readable data (plaintext) into unreadable data (ciphertext) with a key.

Symmetric Asymmetric
Keys One shared secret key for both encrypting and decrypting A key pair: a public key and a private key
Speed Fast: good for large amounts of data Slow: used for small data, key exchange and signatures
Main problem Sharing the key safely Slower; needs a way to trust public keys
Examples AES, 3DES (weak), ChaCha20 RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman (key exchange)

How they work together: a session uses asymmetric cryptography to exchange a key (key exchange), then symmetric encryption for the data (this is what TLS does).

Public key rule: data encrypted with the public key is opened with the private key (confidentiality). A signature is made with the private key and checked with the public key (authenticity).

Exam tip

. Symmetric = fast, one key, bulk data. Asymmetric = two keys, key exchange and signatures. The private key must never be shared. Longer keys are harder to break (key length), for example AES-256 is stronger than AES-128, and RSA needs much longer keys than AES for similar strength.

2Levels of encryption

Where the encryption is applied decides what is protected.

Level Protects Example
Full disk The whole drive, including the operating system BitLocker, a laptop theft
Partition / volume One partition or volume An encrypted data volume
File Individual files An encrypted spreadsheet
Database The database files (transparent encryption) Database at rest
Record Specific rows or fields An encrypted card-number column
Transport / communication Data moving over a network TLS, VPN, IPsec

3Public key infrastructure (PKI) and certificates

A PKI is the system of people, policies and tools that creates, distributes and revokes digital certificates.

Term Meaning
Certificate Binds a public key to an identity, signed by a certificate authority
Certificate authority (CA) The trusted entity that issues and signs certificates
Root of trust The root CA whose certificate devices trust by default; other certificates chain to it
Certificate signing request (CSR) A request that contains the public key and identity details, sent to a CA to get a certificate
Certificate revocation list (CRL) A list of certificates that are no longer valid
Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Real-time check of one certificate's status
Self-signed Signed by its own key: no outside trust, fine for testing
Third-party Issued by a public CA that browsers trust
Wildcard One certificate for all subdomains, such as *.fabrikam.example
Key escrow A trusted third party holds a copy of a private key for recovery
Exam tip

. To get a certificate you create a CSR. To check if it was revoked use CRL (a list) or OCSP (a live query). A self-signed certificate causes browser warnings on the public internet.

4Other cryptographic tools

Tool Purpose Notes
Hashing A one-way fingerprint of data; same input gives the same output Checks integrity; cannot be reversed; algorithms SHA-256, SHA-3; MD5 and SHA-1 are weak
Salting Random data added to a password before hashing Makes identical passwords hash differently and defeats rainbow tables
Digital signature A hash signed with the private key Gives integrity, authentication and non-repudiation
Key exchange A way to agree on a shared key over an open network Diffie-Hellman
Key stretching Slows guessing by repeating hashing many times bcrypt, PBKDF2 Beyond the objectives
Obfuscation Hiding the meaning of data or code Not strong security: steganography, masking, tokenization (module 10)
Tools Hardware and software that manage keys TPM, HSM (hardware security module), key management system

Exam tip

. Hash = integrity, one way. Encryption = confidentiality, reversible with the key. Salt goes into the password hash, it is not secret. A digital signature uses the sender's private key.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors must encrypt a 200 GB database backup quickly. Which type of encryption fits best?

  • AAsymmetric encryption such as RSA only
  • BHashing with SHA-256
  • CA digital signature
  • DSymmetric encryption such as AES
Show the answer

Answer: D. Symmetric encryption is fast and suited to large amounts of data. Hashing is one way and does not allow decryption.

S2A web team needs a certificate for its server. What does it send to the certificate authority?

  • AA certificate revocation list
  • BA private key
  • CA salted hash
  • DA certificate signing request
Show the answer

Answer: D. A CSR holds the public key and identity details. The private key is never sent.

S3A company wants one certificate to cover shop.fabrikam.example and pay.fabrikam.example. Which type fits?

  • ASelf-signed certificate
  • BRoot certificate
  • CWildcard certificate
  • DKey escrow certificate
Show the answer

Answer: C. A wildcard certificate covers all subdomains of a domain.

S4Two users have the same password but their stored hashes differ. What explains this?

  • AKey escrow
  • BTokenization
  • CSalting
  • DObfuscation
Show the answer

Answer: C. A unique salt added before hashing makes identical passwords produce different hashes.

S5Which control gives a recipient proof that a document came from the sender and was not changed?

  • AFull disk encryption
  • BA digital signature
  • CA salted hash alone
  • DA wildcard certificate
Show the answer

Answer: B. A signature made with the sender's private key proves origin and integrity.

S6A browser needs to know right now whether one server certificate has been revoked. Which method gives a live answer?

  • AA downloaded CRL
  • BA CSR
  • COCSP
  • DA self-signed root
Show the answer

Answer: C. OCSP queries the status of a single certificate in real time. A CRL is a list that may be out of date.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How many keys does symmetric encryption use?

Show the answer

One shared secret key.

R2Which key signs a message, and which key verifies it?

Show the answer

The private key signs; the public key verifies.

R3What does a CA do?

Show the answer

Issues and signs digital certificates.

R4CRL or OCSP: which is a live query?

Show the answer

OCSP.

R5What does salting protect against?

Show the answer

Precomputed attacks such as rainbow tables, and identical hashes for identical passwords.

R6Which hardware stores and protects keys?

Show the answer

A hardware security module (HSM) or a TPM.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Symmetric vs asymmetric one key, fast, bulk (AES) vs key pair, slow, key exchange and signatures (RSA, ECC)
Encryption levels full disk, partition, volume, file, database, record, transport
PKI CA issues certificates; CSR requests one; CRL and OCSP check revocation; root of trust; wildcard, self-signed, third-party; key escrow
Hash and salt hash is one way for integrity; salt randomizes password hashes; SHA-256 good, MD5 and SHA-1 weak
Signature hash signed with the private key: integrity, authentication, non-repudiation
